messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's canary routing sync. I sketched a tighter proposal to split decision/control plane from runtime enforcement. Want quick feedback before I turn this into an RFC.

ajay: TLDR? what problem does this solve vs current router?

maria: TLDR: move 'who gets traffic' decisioning to a pluggable, near-stateless policy service. Runtime routers then just enforce assignments. Pros: smaller blast radius for policy rollouts, easier A/B experiments, local router scaling. Cons: extra hop and consistency needs.

sam: extra hop worries me for 99p latency. can routers cache decisions locally to avoid RTT on hot paths?

maria: yes. routers keep a soft cache (TTL + version tag), optimistic reads. decision plane is authoritative and can push invalidations.

leah: ops question: if decision plane flaps, do we fail open or closed? be explicit.

maria: propose fail-safe: on unreachable decision plane, router falls back to deterministic mapping to last-known stable variant. also allow pinned emergency fallback variant.

ajay: session affinity during canaries: sticky cookies or tokens?

sam: cookies ok for browsers, but server->server needs tokens. decision plane issues short-lived session leases cached by router; router prefers token then cache then evaluate.

maria: decision plane APIs: 1) Evaluate (initial assignment + lease issuance), 2) Control stream (delta pushes + invalidations). Router keeps ephemeral leases and an LRU cache.

leah: telemetry: canary decisions need quick SLO signals and quality signals. how do we feed those back?

maria: metrics -> metrics-bridge -> decision plane scorer. decision plane subscribes to rollups (latency, errors, golden prompts) and emits health signals + rollout deltas.

ajay: do we bake ML into decision plane? heavy. alt: keep decision plane rule-based and accept external scores.

maria: keep it agnostic: accept scored inputs and support pluggable scorer. start rule-based, allow swapping in scorer service later.

sam: API sketch: request {request_id, client_id, session_token?, route, context{region,priority}} response {variant, lease_ms, evaluated_at}. Routers treat lease_ms as soft TTL and re-eval in background near expiry.

leah: percent traffic: per-tenant quotas in decision plane or router-weighted hashing?

ajay: hybrid: decision plane issues session assignments and publishes a hashing seed + percentages for non-sticky paths so routers can make local weighted decisions. reduces decision-plane load for stateless high-volume requests.

maria: yes. that keeps decision plane authoritative for sticky sessions while letting routers handle stateless traffic locally.

deploy-bot: canary-proxy image pushed to staging (sha:abc123). smoke tests in 10m.

ajay: observability needs: per-variant SLI dashboards and decision-plane audit logs (who changed what).

maria: include immutable policy revisions, diffs, audit stream to vault, and short-lived rollback API for emergencies.

sam: router currently mixes routing + policy. will this need big rewrite?

maria: incremental: introduce thin policy adapter interface, move logic behind it gradually, compatibility shim for old configs for ~6 months.

leah: propose fallback semantics to document: - default on decision-plane failure: route to last_stable_variant - on degraded health (score < threshold): reduce traffic by multiplier and force synchronous re-eval - on config rollback: drain canary via session expiry rather than immediate kill

ajay: draining by session is ideal. avoids cold starts.

maria: next step: I'll draft RFC covering API surface, lease/caching semantics, telemetry inputs, and migration plan. please comment on the PR when posted.

ajay: will review.

sam: ping me for router shim perf tests.

leah: I'll prepare runbook snippets for decision-plane outage and emergency cutover.

maria: low-effort action: default lease_ms? propose 30s-60s depending on route.

ajay: start 60s default, 10s for critical low-latency routes.

sam: 60s fine; we'll validate with load tests.

maria: thanks all, will post RFC link shortly. :rocket:
